name: REINFORCE
analogy: Think of it as a trader who plays a whole day, then checks the final profit and loss, and tells themselves: repeat the kinds of moves I made on good days a little more, and make the moves from bad days a little less likely. Nothing is judged until the day is over.

steps.title: Play one full episode with the current policy
steps.description: The policy chooses actions bar by bar, sampling each from its own stated chances, until the episode ends. Every state, action and reward along the way is written down.
steps.inExample: The policy trades one full session of 78 five-minute MNQ bars, choosing short, flat or long on every bar, and logs all 78 choices and their rewards.

steps.title: Work out the total outcome from each point onward
steps.description: For every bar, the model adds up all the reward that came from that bar to the end of the episode, giving less weight to far-off reward. This number says how things turned out after that choice.
steps.inExample: The long entered at bar 20 was followed by a total of plus 46 US dollars of reward through the end of the day.

steps.title: Raise or lower the chance of each action taken
steps.description: Each choice is nudged by its outcome. A choice followed by a good total becomes a little more likely in that situation, and a choice followed by a bad total becomes a little less likely. The bigger the outcome, the bigger the nudge.
steps.inExample: Going long at bar 20 becomes slightly more likely in similar situations, while the short at bar 55, followed by minus 31 dollars, becomes less likely.

steps.title: Optionally subtract a typical outcome
steps.description: To cut noise, the average outcome can be subtracted first, so only better-than-usual and worse-than-usual results push the policy. This does not change what is learned on average, only how jumpy the learning is.
steps.inExample: The day's average outcome is plus 5 dollars, so the long at bar 20 is credited with plus 41 rather than plus 46.

steps.title: Repeat with fresh episodes
steps.description: The old episode is discarded, since it was produced by the old policy, and a new episode is played with the improved one. Learning is slow and noisy but needs no estimate of value, only real outcomes.
steps.inExample: After the update the policy plays another session, and over several hundred sessions its average daily reward trends upward.

useFor.task: A first learning baseline in a new trading setup
useFor.example: Checking whether a state made of 35 base features and a simple reward on MNQ bars produces any learnable behaviour before building anything larger.

useFor.task: Strategies with a natural end of episode
useFor.example: Treating each trading day as one episode so the policy is judged on the day's net result after costs.

useFor.task: Rewards that only become clear at the end
useFor.example: Scoring a swing position only when it is closed days later, with no useful reward on the bars in between.

useFor.task: Measuring how noisy learning really is
useFor.example: Running it beside a version with a baseline to see how much steadier the learning curve becomes.

avoidWhen: Episodes are long or data is limited; results swing hugely from one episode to the next, so learning needs very many episodes and a more stable method will get there sooner.
You need feedback within an episode, such as per-bar learning; this method waits for the episode to finish, and a method that estimates value as it goes is a better fit.

example.scenario: A policy has just finished one full trading session on MNQ five-minute bars, 78 bars, ending with a net day of plus 12 US dollars after costs. The model now learns from that single session.

input.summary: The record of one finished session: what the policy saw and did, and the reward on each bar.

fields.name: bars in the session
fields.meaning: The length of the episode being learned from.

fields.name: net result of the session
fields.meaning: The total reward over the episode after trading costs.

fields.name: action at bar 20
fields.meaning: One of the 78 choices, entered after a pullback near 19,380.

fields.name: total reward from bar 20 onward
fields.meaning: How things turned out after that choice, up to the end of the session.

fields.name: total reward from bar 55 onward
fields.meaning: How things turned out after the short.

output.summary: How the policy's chances change in the situations seen in the session.

fields.name: chance of long in the bar 20 situation
fields.meaning: A small rise because the choice was followed by a good result.

fields.name: chance of short in the bar 55 situation
fields.meaning: A small fall because the choice was followed by a bad result.

fields.name: size of one step
fields.meaning: A single session moves the chances only slightly, since one session is a noisy sample.

example.reading: The model's output is a slightly changed policy, not a signal. Watch the average session result over many hundreds of sessions: a rising line means learning is working, while a line that bounces up and down means the noise is swamping the signal.
